messages:
Omar: FYI after the k8s 1.28 rollout in prod we've started seeing GPU nodepools scale down while GPU-backed pods remain Pending. CA logs show nodes marked unneeded immediately after control-plane upgrade. Anyone else seeing this? :warning:
Ben: yep, saw it in us-west-2 g4-pool around 11:12. Pods stuck with `0/1 nodes are available: 1 node(s) had taint {nvidia.com/gpu-preempt=true:NoSchedule}` even though tolerations were present. CA still evicting. :eyes:
Maya: quick check — is cluster-autoscaler version upgraded too? CA behavior changed around taint handling in recent releases. What CA version are we on?
Kai: I'm on it. Ran `kubectl describe node ip-10-0-5-23` and got:
```
Taints: nvidia.com/gpu-preempt=true:NoSchedule
Conditions: Ready True
```
Pods show no matching toleration in their spec (weird, they were stable pre-upgrade).
Ben: here's a snippet from CA logs around the time: `scale_down.go: node ip-10-0-5-23 is unneeded, noNonDaemonPods=true, scaleDownDisabled=false` followed by `drain.go: deleting pod gpu-worker-7` even though pod has toleration in admission controller logs.
infra-bot: Automated job: control-plane-upgrade-prod completed for cluster prod-us-west-2 at 2026-03-17T11:07:33Z.
Julie: This rings a bell — k8s 1.28 removed/changed semantics for `tolerationSeconds` and there was an edge-case where taint effects combined with the CA unsafe eviction path caused eviction of pods that only tolerated taints with `operator: Equal` vs `Exists`. There's an upstream issue: https://github.com/kubernetes/autoscaler/issues/XXXXX (see discussion).
Maya: If toleration matching is different, our mutating webhook that injects tolerations might be producing a shape CA doesn't consider. Can someone paste a failing pod spec?
Kai: failing pod spec (excerpt):
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
spec:
  tolerations:
    - key: "nvidia.com/gpu-preempt"
      operator: "Equal"
      value: "true"
      effect: "NoSchedule"
```
Looks normal. Strange CA path seems to ignore `operator: Equal` here.
Ben: Workarounds discussed: 1) pin GPU nodepool min size to 1 so pool never goes to zero, 2) add a taint-based expander or exclude GPU pools from scale-down, 3) roll back control-plane to 1.27. Tradeoffs: cost vs risk.
Omar: cost note — keeping 1 node per GPU pool across 3 pools (4 GPUs each) in us-west roughly = 3 nodes * $0.75/hr * 24 * 30 = ~$1,620/mo. Not ideal but buys stability while we patch.
Julie: I'll open PR to add a CA config-map override to treat `nvidia.com/*` taints as `DoNotScaleDown` for now. Also adding unit tests for toleration matching edge-case.
Kai: I'll start a canary rollback for prod-us-west-2 to 1.27 in a controlled window. Plan: rollback control-plane only, verify CA behavior, then decide. @sre-oncall can you coordinate the window?
sre-oncall: I can do 12:30-13:30 PST. Will page oncall and add a short incident note. Need to notify customers using EU/GCP since some of our region capacity is limited and cross-region failover might kick in.
deploy-bot: Started rollback job prod-us-west-2/cp-rollback-1782456789 (canary) — status: running. Job: https://deploys.internal/jobs/1782456789
Ben: temporary config snippet to avoid scale-down (apply to CA deployment):
```
--balance-similar-node-groups=false
--ignore-daemonsets-utilization=true
```
Also add `--expander=random` + explicit `--node-group-auto-discovery` filters for gpu pools.
Maya: Another option: change rejecting webhook to ensure tolerations use `operator: Exists` instead of `Equal` for gpu preempt taints so matching is broader. But that's more invasive.
Omar: Action items: 1) Julie PR for CA config to protect gpu-taints (in progress), 2) Kai starts rollback canary (running), 3) Maya to audit mutating webhook for toleration shapes, 4) Ben to estimate cost impact if we set min-size=1 for all gpu pools.
Julie: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler-config/pull/312 — adds taint-protect list + unit tests. :thumbsup:
Kai: Canary rollback complete on control-plane for prod-us-west-2 — monitoring CA logs for 15m.
Ben: after rollback, I see pods no longer evicted and nodes stay around. CA behavior reverted. Looks like control-plane change is the root cause.
Omar: ok good. We'll hold off upgrading other clusters until patch lands in CA or k8s. Keep running canaries and patch webhook if needed.
Julie: filing follow-up to track patch upstream and our permanent mitigation. Ticket INFRA-4238.
Maya: thanks all — please post any residual alerts here. :eyes:
